articles.title: Postgres Retrieval Architecture: Multi-Tenant SaaS Help Center Schema Design
articles.excerpt: Short answer: use a staged retrieval design with explicit collections, bounded queries, and traceable source context, then make index cost a schema input rather than a vendor-selection afterthought. F…
articles.body: Short answer: use a staged retrieval design with explicit collections, bounded queries, and traceable source context, then make index cost a schema input rather than a vendor-selection afterthought. For a gaming help center, the expensive unit is not “an article.” It is every indexed representation of an article section, multiplied by tenant boundaries, locales, active embedding versions, environments, and whatever replication policy the chosen backend requires. A season launch can change hundreds of support sections at once; an item rebalance might change one paragraph for one game and leave every other tenant untouched. Schema design determines whether that edit replaces one retrieval unit or forces a much wider rebuild.

articles.title: Lovable Cloud: What You Actually Get
articles.excerpt: Lovable Cloud is the backend Lovable switches on for you the first time your app needs to save something. Ask for a login page or a table of orders and it appears: a database, auth, file storage, edge…
articles.body: Lovable Cloud is the backend Lovable switches on for you the first time your app needs to save something. Ask for a login page or a table of orders and it appears: a database, auth, file storage, edge functions, a place for API keys. Lovable's docs say it plainly, it runs on Supabase's open-source foundation. So when people ask us "what database does Lovable use", the answer is Postgres, inside a Supabase project that Lovable owns and you rent. That one sentence explains most of what follows, good and bad. What's in the Cloud tab Open your project, go to Cloud, and you get a cut-down Supabase dashboard with Lovable's names on it: Database : your tables, row editing, the RLS policies, and backup restores. Users : who has signed up, and which sign-in methods are on.

articles.title: How to Build a Trade-Rejection Layer for a Polymarket Bot in Python
articles.excerpt: A Polymarket trading bot needs more than a strategy that identifies potential opportunities. It needs a reliable way to reject trades that fail its execution or risk requirements. Without this layer,…
articles.body: A Polymarket trading bot needs more than a strategy that identifies potential opportunities. It needs a reliable way to reject trades that fail its execution or risk requirements. Without this layer, a bot may submit orders using stale market data, accept an unattractive price, exceed its exposure limits, or act on a signal that no longer makes sense. In this tutorial, we'll build a small Python trade-validation layer that evaluates a proposed trade before it reaches the execution component. The implementation is deliberately independent of any specific Polymarket SDK. That makes it easier to test the decision logic without connecting a wallet, signing orders, or risking real funds.

articles.title: Build an invoice-extraction pilot that cannot write to the accounting ledger
articles.excerpt: A small-business team wants less manual entry. Connecting an extractor directly to the ledger turns an extraction experiment into an operational decision. Start with a separate review table instead. S…
articles.body: A small-business team wants less manual entry. Connecting an extractor directly to the ledger turns an extraction experiment into an operational decision. Start with a separate review table instead. Supply text before extraction. A text PDF and a scan require different upstream steps; a scan needs OCR. n8n’s Information Extractor accepts text and a schema. Define explicit fields: vendor, invoice reference, subtotal, tax and total. Retain the source document reference so a reviewer can compare the values. Route extracted values to a draft table. In this pilot, do not connect a ledger-write node or payment trigger. Mark every record PENDING_REVIEW. Record checks separately: vendor match, amount review, and comparison with purchase orders, receipts and prior invoice records.

articles.title: The artifact worth reviewing when agents write the code
articles.excerpt: GitHub's Security Lab reported 24 Android vulnerabilities found by an AI security agent, and the part worth copying is what ended up version-controlled. Not the exploit code. The set of YAML taskflows…
articles.body: GitHub's Security Lab reported 24 Android vulnerabilities found by an AI security agent, and the part worth copying is what ended up version-controlled. Not the exploit code. The set of YAML taskflows that guided the model through the audit, checked into a public repository, runnable by anyone with a Copilot license. The agent did the finding. The taskflows are the thing a team can read, diff, and argue about. That is a small shift with a large consequence for review. When a person writes a patch, the diff is a decent summary of the judgment that went into it, because the person held the reasoning and the code is the residue. When an agent writes the patch, the reasoning lives somewhere else entirely: a prompt, a rule file, a model version, a sequence of tool calls.

articles.body: Algumas regras de negócio não são só código. São fórmulas. Fórmulas complexas, agregações pesadas, fórmulas que contam a história de um processo inteiro. Na maioria dos casos, a regra pode estar certa. Está no papel e está na classe de negócio. Mas onde estão os passos? A prática comum é guardar apenas o resultado final. O certo é guardar os passos até ao resultado: a fórmula com cada parte, os operadores, os valores intermediários e descrições relevantes. Qual é a solução? Breakdown de Fórmulas. Conceito Em vez de o sistema guardar somente total = 5000, ele guarda o processo completo. Essa técnica torna-se a única fonte da verdade. Cada parte do sistema pega no que precisa desse breakdown: uma parte vai para a BD, outra é libertada no front, outra alimenta o fluxo de negócio.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 13, 1773: Astronomer Charles Messier discovers the Whirlpool Galaxy before we ever knew it was a galaxy
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 13, 1773, a French astronomer named Charles Messier discovered the "Whirlpool Galaxy," also known as Messier 51, or M51. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 13, 1773, a French astronomer named Charles Messier discovered the " Whirlpool Galaxy , " also known as Messier 51, or M51. Charles Messier was scanning the sky for objects that could confuse comet hunters when he catalogued the galaxy as M51. However, Messier wasn't able to see the spiral structure, and he didn't identify it as a galaxy. Seventy-two years later, another astronomer named William Parsons saw the whirlpool shape, but he thought it was a spiral nebula. Eventually, Edwin Hubble found out that M51 and other features like it were actually galaxies. Spiral galaxy M51 (NGC 5194), The Whirlpool Galaxy, displays its long arms which consist of stars and gas laced with dust arranged in long lanes, in this view from the Hubble Space Telescope.

articles.title: 'We basically did Top Gun in space': 'Star Trek Starfleet Academy' warps back into action in March 2027 for sophomore year in the final frontier
articles.excerpt: The sophomore season of "Star Trek: Starfleet Academy" will warp back to the small screen in March 2027 when the limited series returns for its final season on Paramount+.
articles.body: NEW YORK — Set your phasers to back-to-school, space fans. Star Trek is going back to Starfleet Academy for season 2, and we finally have a release date. The sophomore season of " Star Trek: Starfleet Academy " will warp back to the small screen in March 2027 when the limited series returns for its final season on Paramount+ . The series, which follows a class of cadets balancing Starfleet classes, space adventures (and yes, some love) in the 32nd century, will return with its full cast and even add new faces, showrunners announced at a panel at New York Comic Con 2026 on Saturday (Oct. 10). "Season one is about letting go of who you were in the past to start again at Starfleet Academy," executive producer and co-showrunner Noga Landau said in the Star Trek panel.

articles.title: See the original Galileo shuttle from 'Star Trek' in its new home at the Original Series Set Tour in New York
articles.excerpt: This iconic spaceship will now live long and prosper in its brand-new Star Trek Tour home.
articles.body: Nostalgia is a hell of a thing, especially when it comes to sci-fi. For "Star Trek" fans wanting to mark the franchise's 60th anniversary this year, a geeky pilgrimage to upstate New York should be on the cards. Why? Because alongside the splendid autumnal colors, they can steer over to Ticonderoga to behold the newly installed Galileo shuttlecraft. After a complete two-year restoration project in 2012 headed up by superfan and collector Adam Schneider, this iconic fictional spacecraft, seen by millions in seven episodes over three seasons of "Star Trek: The Original Series," was recently relocated from its former home at the Johnson Space Center Museum in Houston, Texas.

articles.title: Earth's poles shifted surprisingly fast during the age of dinosaurs, ancient sea levels reveal
articles.excerpt: The location of Earth's geographic poles has changed several times over the past 320 million years in a process known as true polar wander.
articles.body: The location of Earth's geographic poles has changed several times over the past 320 million years in a process known as true polar wander, according to measurements of ancient flooding brought about by sea level changes resulting from our planet's crust shifting relative to Earth's spin axis. Such a shift can affect climate, both on local scales and globally, as regions that were by the poles find themselves moving down to lower latitudes and vice versa. This can then affect atmospheric circulation patterns, which affect climate across the world. The changes would have affected the environments in which life developed and evolved, from the age of the dinosaurs through to some of our oldest primate ancestors.
